White field; left the shocked open-mouthed cartoon man; center a cracked green piggy bank with X eyes sitting inside an open steel bear trap, bills draining from a spout into a sewer grate; red warning triangle; heavy black "BE CAREFUL / WITH THIS..." with a curved arrow. script.opening_words:
Denise and Patrick hit $2.4 million
on a Tuesday afternoon in March. Patrick
printed the spreadsheet. Denise stuck it
to the refrigerator under a magnet
shaped like a lobster. Both 52 years old
and the tab at the bottom said $96,000
a year for every 26 years of maxing the
401k and driving a Camry with 190,000
miles on it and they had made it. And
then 3 weeks after Patrick turned in his
badge, a health insurance quote showed
up in the mail for $2
script.ending_words:
m with
somebody who does this professionally.
And if you want to go deeper, our school
community link is still below. So,
here's the question worth carrying out
of this video.
It is not how much do I need. That one
has been asked to death, and it produces
a number that goes on a refrigerator and
stops being useful the day you actually
stop working. The better question is
this, at what income am I going to
choose to live and what does that one
number cost me? Because the number you
saved is a headline. The number you show
on paper every year is the one that
quietly writes the rest of your life.
script.analysis: All 18,919 stored characters read in two contiguous ranges with canonical hash match. Story hook: Denise and Patrick reach $2.4M at 52, then a $2,100/month health quote; subscribe CTA. Context: SCF top-10% threshold and median; traps triggered by income not net worth. Sections: Bengen 1994/Trinity, Kitces 45-year ~3.5%, Morningstar 3.9%; sequence risk (1966 retiree); CAPE ~41 vs median ~17; 13 years before Medicare and expired enhanced ACA credits; KFF cliff example ($62K vs $64K); 400% FPL couple ~$84,600; spending cascade to ~$42K; mid-video community CTA; Roth conversions and 0% gains vs subsidy; IRMAA two-year lookback; MAGI as the controllable number. Counterarguments: guardrails (>5% in some Morningstar cases), Blanchett spending smile, EBRI under-spending and guaranteed-income floor. Sonia's early long-term care purchase, Fidelity $345K excluding LTC, nursing-home costs, adult-child support, Social Security 35-year average, 2033 trust fund, NIIT unindexed; resolution: choose $78K income plus part-time consulting; disclaimer and second CTA. Exceptionally well-sourced, balanced and structurally strong. ASR not audio-verified.

claim_audit: 0:9500 SCF 2022: top-10% net worth threshold ~$1.94M, median ~$192,900, mean >$1M - consistent. Bengen 1994 and Trinity 1998 correctly dated; Kitces horizon extension to ~3.5% and Morningstar 3.9% (30-year) consistent with published work. $3M x 4% = $120K vs 3.5% = $105K; $2.4M x 4% = $96K vs 3.5% = $84K - correct. 1966 retiree sequence example consistent with standard illustrations. CAPE ~41 near record outside 1999 consistent with mid-2026 levels (approximate).

0:9500 Enhanced ACA premium tax credits expiring after 2025 restores the 400% FPL cliff; KFF-style example: $62,000 x ~9.96% = ~$515/month vs ~$1,244 unsubsidized, ~$8,750/year difference - consistent arithmetic. 400% FPL for a two-person household (2025 guideline $21,150) = $84,600 correct; $96K is ~$11.4K over. Cascade $84K - $25K - $11K - tax = ~$42K is illustrative; MAGI from portfolio withdrawals depends on account types and basis (Roth and cost basis are not income), which the script addresses later via MAGI planning.

9500:18919 2026 0% long-term capital gains bracket up to ~$98,900 taxable income (MFJ) correct; Roth conversions and realized gains count toward MAGI correct; IRMAA two-year lookback correct. Guardrail strategies supporting higher starting rates, Blanchett spending smile and EBRI finding (~12% of assets spent in first 20 years by $500K+ retirees; about a third grew assets) consistent with sources. Fidelity ~$345K couple estimate excludes pre-65 and long-term care, correct; ~70% LTC need and ~$127K private nursing room consistent with HHS/Genworth figures. Adult-child support (~half of parents, ~$1,400/month) consistent with recent surveys. Social Security 35-year averaging and 2033/77% trustees projection correct; NIIT thresholds unindexed since 2013 correct.
